cohort: The study included 8053 'term' singleton deliveries of live-born newborns recruited from 13 hospitals in Sri Lanka over 2 months in 2023.
finding: Neonates born at 38 weeks showed better outcomes than those born at 37 weeks, with 37-week deliveries associated with higher rates of maternal comorbidities and inferior neonatal outcomes including lower APGAR scores, increased resuscitation needs, and higher intensive care admission rates.
mod_finding: The elective caesarean section rate was highest at 37 weeks (43.4%) compared to 38 weeks (31.1%) or higher gestations.
